note: A three-note tune from the tab, then tunes of your own from its notes over a drone on the home note. Moves holds any key, so the text names the home note as a degree and the drone's key as a param, and the last block makes the drill the player's own.

exercise.title: A three-note tune, then your own
exercise.why: A tune sounds finished when it ends on its home note, so the three notes of this tune and that ending are enough to make up tunes of your own.

cells.text:
Press Play below to hear the tune, then play along from the tab.
Practice until your fingers find its three notes without the tab.

Press Play below to start the drone on {{=key}}. Make up short tunes from the three notes of the tune above, in any order and any rhythm, and end each one on the tune's last note, {{1}}, the drone's own note.
Then end one on another note, and listen for the difference: one ending sounds finished, the other sounds on its way somewhere.
{{?key}}In another key the three notes sit on other frets, and the home note is still the tune's last note.
